title: Flying With a French Bulldog: Airline Rules, Cabin Size and Risks
description: Flying with a French Bulldog: why Frenchies can't fly cargo, American, Delta and Alaska cabin rules, carrier size, CDC entry rules and tips for a safe flight.

faq.q: Can French Bulldogs fly on planes?
faq.a: Yes, but usually only in the cabin. As of November 2026, American, Delta and Alaska do not accept snub-nosed dogs in cargo, so your Frenchie must fit in a carrier under the seat. Confirm the current rules with your airline when you book.

faq.q: Can French Bulldogs fly in cargo?
faq.a: Major US airlines including American, Delta and Alaska do not allow it. Short-nosed dogs have a higher risk of heatstroke and breathing problems under stress or heat, and about half of 122 airline-related dog deaths in DOT data released in 2010 involved short-faced breeds.

faq.q: Can a French Bulldog fit under an airplane seat?
faq.a: Smaller Frenchies can. US airlines such as American cap soft-sided carriers at about 18 by 11 by 11 inches, and the dog must stay in it under the seat for the whole flight. Many adults, which can weigh up to 28 lb, are too big to fit comfortably.

faq.q: Should I sedate my French Bulldog for a flight?
faq.a: No. The AVMA advises against tranquilizers for air travel. Talk to your vet before giving any medication.

faq.q: What does my dog need to come back into the US?
faq.a: Since August 1, 2024, the CDC requires every dog entering the US to look healthy, be at least 6 months old, be microchipped and have a CDC Dog Import Form receipt. Dogs that have been in high-risk rabies countries need more.
